requestedActions.title: List repository names visible to the connected person, including pagination

guide.summary: Forgejo documents an authorization-code OAuth2 provider where user-consented apps act for the connected person. OAuth tokens are unscoped and can run any action the user can, so no OAuth permission identifier applies; the boundary is the person's own repository access.
guide.recommendation: The requested API test is not ready yet. Resolve the access mapping for List repository names visible to the connected person, including pagination. Use “Find missing request” or add official documentation beside that action.

findings.title: Forgejo documents an OAuth2 provider with the Authorization Code Grant and PKCE
findings.detail: Forgejo acts as an OAuth2 provider so third-party apps can access resources with user consent. It supports the Authorization Code Grant with PKCE, and both confidential and public client types.
findings.appliesWhen: The customer's own Forgejo instance is used as the OAuth2 provider for individual customer accounts.

evidence.quote: OAuth2 provider Forgejo supports acting as an OAuth2 provider to allow third party applications to access its resources with the user’s consent.
Supported OAuth2 Grants At the moment, Forgejo only supports the Authorization Code Grant standard with additional support for the following extensions:
Client types Forgejo supports both confidential and public client types, as defined by RFC 6749 .

findings.title: OAuth2 tokens are unscoped and can run any action on behalf of the user
findings.detail: Scopes are not implemented for OAuth2 tokens, and they can be used to execute any action on behalf of the user, not just Git actions. The documented boundary is therefore the connected person's own access, and the read-only restriction must be enforced by the app.
findings.appliesWhen: The app uses an OAuth2 token from Forgejo's provider to call the REST API.

evidence.quote: OAuth2 scopes are not yet implemented.
Note Scopes are not implemented for OAuth2 tokens and they can be used to
execute any actions on behalf of the user, not just Git-related actions.

findings.title: OAuth access tokens are accepted by the API as Bearer tokens
findings.detail: Access tokens from Forgejo's OAuth2 provider are accepted by the Authorization: Bearer header, and by token or access_token query parameters. Requests then use the connected user's access.
findings.appliesWhen: The app calls the repository search endpoint with an OAuth access token.

evidence.quote: OAuth2 Provider Access tokens obtained from Forgejo’s OAuth2 provider are accepted by these methods:
Authorization: Bearer ... header in HTTP headers
token=... parameter in URL query string

findings.title: Customer registers an OAuth2 application and completes the authorization flow
findings.detail: The app must be registered in user settings with its redirect configuration, and the connected person must authorize it to obtain tokens. The token request must use the same redirect URI as the authorize request.
findings.appliesWhen: Each customer organization or workspace connects its own Forgejo account.

evidence.quote: OpenID Connect (OIDC) To use the Authorization Code Grant as a third-party application, it is required to register a new application via the “Settings” ( /user/settings/applications ) section. To test

It is possible for any user to manually register a new OAuth2 application on the /user/settings/applications page for the purpose of using Git credential helpers different from the pre-registered ones.
The REDIRECT_URI in the access_token request must match the REDIRECT_URI in the authorize request.

steps.title: Register the OAuth2 application on the customer's Forgejo instance
steps.detail: Using the customer's own instance, create an OAuth2 application at /user/settings/applications with a redirect URI for the app, choosing one client type (confidential, with client secret) for the first test. Record the Client ID and Client secret.
steps.doneWhen: The application appears in the user's application settings with a Client ID and a secret was recorded.

It is possible for any user to manually register a new OAuth2 application on the /user/settings/applications page for the purpose of using Git credential helpers different from the pre-registered ones.
Client types Forgejo supports both confidential and public client types, as defined by RFC 6749 .

fields: INSTANCE_BASE_URL: customer's full HTTPS Forgejo origin, user-provided

steps.title: Send the user to the consent page and verify the callback
steps.detail: Redirect the connected person to the documented authorization endpoint. They sign in and approve the app; Forgejo redirects to REDIRECT_URI with code and state. The app checks that state matches what it sent.
steps.doneWhen: The callback at REDIRECT_URI returns a code parameter and the returned state matches the sent state.

evidence.quote: https://[ YOUR-FORGEJO-URL ]/login/oauth/authorize?client_id=CLIENT_ID&redirect_uri=REDIRECT_URI&response_type=code&state=STATE The CLIENT_ID can be obtained by registering an application in the settings. The STATE is a random string that will be
The user will now be asked to authorize your application. If they authorize it, the user will be redirected to the REDIRECT_URL , for example:
sent back to your application after the user authorizes. The state parameter is optional but should be used to prevent CSRF attacks.

fields: STATE: random string generated by the app
INSTANCE_BASE_URL: your full HTTPS instance URL, without a trailing slash

steps.title: Exchange the authorization code for an access token
steps.detail: Post the returned code to the access token endpoint with the same REDIRECT_URI, client credentials and authorization_code grant. Store access_token for later API calls.
steps.doneWhen: The response contains access_token and token_type bearer.

steps.title: Request the first page of visible repositories
steps.detail: Call the repository search endpoint with the Bearer token and limit to read the first page. The private parameter is left at its documented default so private repositories the user can access are included. Repository names are read from the data array.
steps.doneWhen: The response returns ok true and a data array; each entry's name field is read and the Link header and x-total-count are captured. Boundary check: inspect the actual grant against the documented access above; confirm the outgoing request log contains only the requested operations and no prohibited actions.

steps.title: Confirm the token is read-only in practice and cannot create repositories
steps.detail: Use a safe nonmutating check: request a read of a repository the user can see, and confirm the app code never sends POST, PUT, PATCH or DELETE to repository routes. OAuth tokens are unscoped, so enforcement is by the app, not the token.
steps.doneWhen: Outgoing request log shows only GET requests to /api/v1/repos/search and no repository write requests.

steps.title: Follow the next page link until the last page
steps.detail: Repeat the same search with page incremented, preserving limit, using the Link header next URL as returned. Stop when the response has no rel="next" link or the page is past x-total-count.
steps.doneWhen: All pages are read until no rel="next" link remains, and the total matches x-total-count. Boundary check: inspect the actual grant against the documented access above; confirm the outgoing request log contains only the requested operations and no prohibited actions.

evidence.quote: Pagination The API supports pagination. The page and limit parameters are used to specify the page number and the number of items per page. As well, the Link header is
< link: < https://forgejo.example.org/api/v1/repos/search ? limit = 1 &page = 2 > ; rel = "next", < https://forgejo.example.org/api/v1/repos/search? limit = 1 &page = 5252 > ; rel = "last"
returned with the next, previous, and last page links if there are more than one page. The x-total-count is also returned to indicate the total number of items.

fields: NEXT_PAGE_URL: literal Link header rel=next value from the prior response, resolved against the same HTTPS instance host
